text.en:
1. This Ordinance may be cited as the Coin (Import
and Export) Ordinance, 1957.

2. In this Ordinance—

"banker" means any corporation carrying on the
business of bankers or ‘financial agents in the
Federation;

"money-changer" means a person who carries on
the business of money-changing as his chief business.

(b) the exportation from the Federation of such
coins, being legal tender within the Federa-
tion, as are in such order specified;

(c) the circulation in the Federation of such
foreign coins, not being legal tender within
the Federation, as are in such order specified.

(2) TAN                  may by order published

exportation from the Federation of such coins as are
in such order specified.

(3) The provisions of any order made under sub-
section (1) shall not extend to the importation or
exportation by any person of any copper or bronze
coin the aggregate nominal value whereof is less than
five doHars or of any silver coin the aggregate nominal

(2) In any case in which it has been proved to the

(4) Any person importing or exporting coin under
the provision of any such licence shall be bound to
comply with the terms in such licence specified, and
any person importing or exporting coin in contraven-

contained in sub-section (2) shall apply in the case of
any coin exported in contravention of the terms of any
such licence.

(5) If any person shall in contravention of any such
order circulate or attempt to circulate any coin in such
order specified, he shall be liable to a fine not exceed-
ing fifty dears, and the coin shall be forfeited.     dg yat tg

deemed to circulate coin who gives such coin to a
banker or money-changer in exchange for other coin
or for notes.

5. If any coin the circulation of which in the Federa-
tion is prohibited by any order made under this Ordi-
nance is found within the Federation otherwise than
in the possession of a banker or money-changer after
the expiration of thirty days from the publication of
such order it may be forfeited, and it may be seized
without warrant by any police officer and detained
pending the declaration of a First Class Magistrate as
to its forfeiture.

6. Any Magistrate who is satisfied by sworn
information in writing that there is good reason to
believe that any coin which has been imported or is
in the act of being imported or exported in contraven-
tion of any such order as aforesaid is likely to be found
in any place to the nominal value of fifty dellars or
upwards, may by warrant under his hand direct any
public officer named or specified therein to enter such
place and search the same and seize all coin or coins
found therein the importation or exportation of which
is for the time being prohibited as aforesaid, and detain
the same pending the declaration of a First Class
Magistrate as to its forfeiture.

7. Any person reasonably suspected of any contra-
vention of the provisions of this Ordinance may be
arrested by any police officer without warrant.

8. (1) Forfeitures of coin under this Ordinance may
be declared by a First Class Magistrate in all cases
where a person is convicted of an offence against this
Ordinance in respect thereof, on the conviction of such
person, or where no person is convicted, within three
months of the seizure of such coin.

(2) An appeal to a Judge of the High Court at the
instance of any person interested shall lie from a
declaration of forfeiture of coin. Notice of appeal shall
be given within one month of the pronouncement of
the declaration of forfeiture.

9. The convicting Magistrate may direct any fine or
any portion of a fine imposed and levied under this
Ordinance to be paid to the informer or informers.

10. All orders and notifications published or con-
tinued in force under any written law repealed by this
Ordinance which were in force immediately before the
commencement of this Ordinance shall continue in
force as if such orders or notifications had been orders
made and published under this Ordinance.

11. The Coin Import and Export Enactment of the
Federated Malay States and the Coin Ordinance of
the Straits Settlements are hereby repealed.
